user_reported_bug: Security Audit SEC-004 [MEDIUM]: Unescaped user-supplied IVR labels/greetings/messages/action strings interpolated into HTML-parse-mode Telegram messages. A malicious or accidental label like `Sales <script>alert("x")</script> & "Support"` would either break the Telegram HTML parser (message send fails with `Bad Request: can't parse entities`) or corrupt the render. Reported by the security_audit_agent against files: js/phone-config.js (ivrMenu + ivrAnalyticsReport, all 4 locales), js/_index.js (_renderSubMenuOverview + Twilio submenu notification + rename-prompt), js/voice-service.js (Telnyx submenu notification).
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Focused SEC-004 backend verification passed: /dev/ivr-multilayer-test returned pass:true with step10_label_in_menu, step11_label_in_analytics, and step12_escape_helper all ok; snippets contained <script>, &, " and no raw <script>. Regression endpoints /dev/ivr-audio-library-integrity and /dev/ivr-audio-preview-rename also returned pass:true. Additional direct renderer test verified phone-config ivrMenu and ivrAnalyticsReport escape hostile greeting/label/message/key/action content across en/fr/zh/hi.

No remaining raw option.label interpolation was found in the reported surfaces.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Focused test plan used: verify the exact SEC-004 Telegram HTML escaping bug; inspect changed files and git status; prove helper/menu/analytics snippets escape the hostile label and no raw < appears outside intended Telegram tags; verify all four phone-config locales directly; run multi-layer IVR and audio regression dev endpoints. rca_of_the_issue: Previously, user-controlled IVR labels/greetings/messages/actions could be interpolated directly into Telegram parse_mode:'HTML' messages. The fix centralizes HTML escaping for &, <, >, and " and applies it to the reported render/notification surfaces.
